_about: Where a portal may be placed, and how big it is. Enhanced's portals.json has a
'placement' block and marks it _guess, saying so outright: its _radius_note reads
'Binary has g_portalCollisionRadius / portalCollisionRadius; value unknown.' These
are the decoded answers, and they replace that block's radius the way transit.json
'What the decode leaves for later steps'.
TWO radii, not one. The port carried a single collision_radius_px and used it for
both a placed portal's own trigger and the circle in which an antiportal refuses a
tap. They are unrelated: the first is a constant, the second is half the field

_source: Portal.angelscript, bytes 297250..297291: g_portalCollisionRadius = 14. The
PortalManager's constructor stores getScale() * 14 (bytes 297250.., instruction
111-113), and one scale unit is one of the port's pixels - preLoop calls
updateScaleFactor(256) and the port's view is 256 px tall - so it is 14 of them.
This is the circle a traveller enters a placed portal by. It is NOT what refuses
a tap near an antiportal.
_perish_source: ETHCallback_portal (Portal.angelscript, bytes 359141..359885) #12-86, the placed portal's own
per-frame callback. It keeps a uint elapsedTime on the entity: #22-37 set it to 0 on the first
call, #38-53 AddToUInt(getLastFrameElapsedTime()) on every later one - so the first frame
contributes NOTHING. #65 CMPIu elapsedTime, 20000 with #66 JNP past the block, so the portal is
killed once the total is ABOVE 20000 ms, and #67-79 skip that when uint dontPerish is non-zero.
dontPerish IS SET BY EXACTLY ONE SCENE, and it is not a level: scenes/loading_screen.esc carries
<Type>uint</Type><Name>dontPerish</Name><Value>1</Value> in the CustomData of its own entity named
'portal' (the same portal.png system, lifeTime 100, size 64, beside float speed 1 and stride 2),
so the loading screen's portal is the one portal in the game that stands for ever. NO LEVEL SCENE
and none of the 190 .ent files names it, and insertPortal never sets it on a portal a shot opens,
so every portal the PLAYER opens perishes 20 seconds after it opened. ETHEntity::GetUInt of a name
that is not there returns 0 (ETHEntity.cpp:865-870), which is what those portals read.
ALL 323 .ent AND .esc FILES ARE UTF-16: a plain grep over them finds nothing at all, and this line
said 'never set' until the census was re-run with a BOM-aware reader.
THE PORT'S CLOCK IS ITS TICK, not a rendered frame: 60 a second, frozen with the level under a
pause, which is what the original's own callback does while STimeManager is paused (its
m_factor is 0, the same factor unitsPerSecond and this port's motions read).
This is the visuals plan's R14, decided as the original does (00_order section 6).

_source: ETHCallback_portal #1-10 calls linearMotion(thisEntity, vertical true, angle 0f, startAngle 0f)
first thing every frame - its arguments pushed last-first (00_order 8.0 rule 3): #1 and #2 push
the two 0f, #3-4 push SetV1 v3, v1, the 8-bit immediate 1, and #5-9 push the entity.
speed and stride are portal.ent's own <CustomData>, which linearMotion reads off the entity
(#41-51, #100-110): float speed 1, float stride 2.
So a placed portal HOVERS: y = where it opened + 2 x cos(t radians), one radian a second, a
6.28 s period, starting at its lowest point (cos 0 = +1 and the level's +y is down).
MEASURED in the original at 16 fps: amplitude 1.95 and 1.89 u on the two portals of a 1-3 pair,
omega 1.012 and 0.998 rad/s (out/parity/footage/F2.md section 4.1, 'Placed-portal bob').
IT IS ONE POINT AND NOT TWO. linearMotion ends in SetPosition (#205-208), and
PortalManager::doTeleporting reads that same GetPositionXY, so the circle a traveller enters by
hovers with the picture. 00_order 8.15 R25 states the rule for a carrier's point; this is the
same rule for a portal's.
PortalManager's constructor sets FIRST_PORTAL_MIN_TIME = 300 and
NEXT_PORTAL_MIN_TIME = 400 (bytes 137xxx, instructions 134-140). Enhanced's
portals.json carries 0.0 s and 0.25 s and admits them: 'The names are real; the
numbers are invented.' These are the real ones, in milliseconds.
THEY GATE TWO DIFFERENT THINGS.
first_ms gates the whole tap-reading path. PortalManager::update (bytes
138545..139692) jumps past managePortalInsertion when the game is paused, or
finished, or gameTimer.getTime() < FIRST_PORTAL_MIN_TIME. Both timers are
built in the PortalManager's constructor and a manager is built per level, so
this is 300 ms from the START OF EVERY LEVEL, not once per session.
next_ms gates ONE TAP, inside managePortalInsertion (bytes 143178..144166),
after hasPortalRequestInput and the touch position: the tap proceeds only when
lastPortalTimer.getTime() > NEXT_PORTAL_MIN_TIME.
RESET ON ACCEPTANCE, NOT ON SUCCESS. Timer::reset on lastPortalTimer runs at
instruction 78, BEFORE SeekEntity('projectile.ent') and before
computePortalFinalPos reports hasFailed. So a shot that flies off and opens
nothing still spends the 400 ms.
That does not contradict the owner's 'a failed shot costs nothing' (11
September): that is about the portal BUDGET, which a failed shot does not spend
and the port already gets right. The firing rate is a separate thing, and the
script is unambiguous about it. Do not make one match the other.
_both_start_at_zero: Timer's constructor calls its own reset (Timer.angelscript, bytes
38787..38883 and 39242..39299), update adds getLastFrameElapsedTime, and a
PortalManager - with both Timers - is built per level. So gameTimer and
lastPortalTimer are BOTH at zero when a level begins, and the first tap of a
level is held off by the LARGER of the two: 400 ms, not 300. That is the
original's behaviour, not an artefact of this port.
The comparisons differ and the port copies each: update refuses while gameTimer
is BELOW first_ms, managePortalInsertion proceeds only when lastPortalTimer is
ABOVE next_ms - so it refuses on equal.

_source: A SHOT IS FIRED WHEN A TOUCH COMES UP, and only a touch that stayed within scale(18) of where it
went down (the remaster record's step 137).
hasPortalRequestInput (Portal.angelscript, bytes 353953..354113) #1-9: getTouchState(t, ignoreStatus)
CMPIi 3, and anything but 3 returns false. 3 is GSKS_RELEASE (reference/ethanon
toolkit/Source/src/gs2d/src/Input/KeyStateManager.h:33), and KeyStateManager::Update
(KeyStateManager.cpp:33-57) gives it on the ONE frame after the last one the touch was held:
GSKS_HIT on the first held frame, GSKS_DOWN on the rest, GSKS_RELEASE on the first frame up.
#10-22: then getMaxMoveLength(t) CMPf scale(18), TNP: true when the move is AT MOST scale(18).
TouchInputManager::update (bytes 159141..159915), every frame: on GSKS_HIT (#60-104)
maxMoveLength[t] = 0 and hitPos[t] = the touch; on HIT or DOWN (#41-50) lastTouchPos[t] = the
touch (#105-117) and maxMoveLength[t] = max(maxMoveLength[t], distance(hitPos[t], touch))
(#118-152). So the move is the FARTHEST the touch has been from where it went down, over the
frames it was held, not the length of its path; the release frame adds nothing.
managePortalInsertion (PortalManager.angelscript, bytes 143178..144166) #16-25 asks
hasPortalRequestInput(t, false) of every touch, and #26-41 aims at getReleasePos(t)
(bytes 161662..161825: lastTouchPos[t], the last point the touch was HELD at) plus
GetCameraPos() on the release frame (getAbsolutePos, bytes 316167..316280). The two gates
(cooldowns above), the pads' and the buttons' tests (ScreenPad::isValidPoint,
PortalManager::isValidPoint -> UILayerManager::isPointInButton) are all asked of that release
point on that frame. blockPortalEffects (budget 0, no_budget below) #35-60 asks the same.
getTouchState (bytes 161450..161662) answers GSKS_UP for a touch a help block or a lift disabled
(touchEnabled false, set true again once the touch is up), so neither fires on its release.
scale() is the script's SGlobalScale, screenHeight / 256 (00_order 8.0 rule 5), and the port's view
is 256 units tall (view.json), so scale(18) is 18 units of the view, in a window of any size.
FOOTAGE agrees: F14, F15 and F16, each in its section 1 ('the shot fires on touch-up'; monkey touch
down, then up 0.10-0.11 s later).
WHAT THE ORIGINAL WORKS OUT AT THE TAP: computePortalFinalPos, the global (PortalManager.angelscript,
bytes 355236..356384) and PortalManager's method over it (141090..142200), read in 00_order section 8.4
(decode D3 with D3_check, which wins) and re-read for the visuals plan's 10.1 (planning step 103).
It decides `willDie` - so red_cross or portal_mark at the tap - whether red_waves (A) is added, and
WHERE THE SHOT GOES: the shot's destiny is its finalPos, and it opens a portal there or fails there
(ETHCallback_projectile #127-272). Until planning step 156 the port read it for the pictures only (the
owner's standing ruling R15) and flew its own shot to the tap; the owner's ruling of the program is
that the original decides, and the shot now flies by this block (Portals::State::Shoot, R23).
ray_start_units: global #5-28, origin = normalize(destPos - casterPos) x g_scale.scale(8): the ray
starts 8 units out from the caster, along the aim.
ray_ignores: global #30-51, the string GetClosestContact is given, one name per entry, matched
exactly against an entity's name (ETHEntityChooser.cpp:43-61), so a level's bare `death_area` is
NOT ignored where `death_area.ent` is. Every other body counts, a sensor as well as a solid one
(ETHRayCastCallback.cpp:40-50 asks only the chooser).
push_units: global #194-248, jumpForth = normalize(destPos - casterPos) x g_scale.scale(10), +10
past a teleportable body's contact and -10 short of a static one a reflected shot meets; the
position a reflected shot's mark is added at (ETHCallback_reflect_agent #216-235).
retry_from_units, retry_back_units: the method's head-height retry, #123-146 nextTry = origin +
g_scale.scale(vector2(0, -30)) and #194-217 nextTry -= normalize(destPos - nextTry) x
g_scale.scale(6), run when the first ray failed or ended on a body with nothing at the tap
(shouldTryToAvoidTeleportableEntity 140931..141090 #3-24) and nothing but that body at nextTry
(#148-189). Both tests are EntityGrabber(point, 0, grabAllObstacles) (EntityGrabber::EntityGrabber
23924..24990 #66-212, grabAllObstacles 361404..361475 returns true for any entity): every body
whose shape holds the point, sensors included. #231-236 write the retry's hasFailed whatever it
is, and #242-251 keep the retry's position only when it did not fail (D3_check B).
fire_diamond_reach: the method's fire-diamond branch (#21-64), which casts no ray and never writes
*hasFailed: it returns origin + (destPos - origin) x g_scale.scale(64) - 64 times the tap's offset,
with the factor at 1.0 (D3 section 1, 'Scale convention') - so the shot is aimed far out and the
burn (turnProjectilesIntoFireBalls) takes it before it can arrive (D3 section 3).
PortalManager::blockPortalEffects (137862..138545), which PortalManager::update calls instead of
managePortalInsertion when maxPortals is 0 (#48-56): on a tap, and only while the no_portal_sign
handle the constructor cached is not null (#80-92; ctor 135924..136705 #118-132
SeekEntity('no_portal_sign.ent'), by the NAME, one spelling), red_waves.ent at the tap and
startEarthquake(7, 40) - earthquake.json's no_portal_tap row. It returns at once on
scenes/level0.esc (#3-20), which places no sign anyway: max_portals is 0 on level0, level6a, level14
and level27a, and the last three are the three that place the sign (1-15, 2-07, 2-28). There is no
400 ms gate on this path, and at most one wave a frame (#137-138 return).
isPointInAntiPortalField (AntiPortalManager.angelscript, bytes 334800..335020):
r = entity.GetSize().x * 0.5
return squaredDistance(entity.GetPositionXY(), p) < r * r
so the radius is half the FIELD ENTITY'S OWN SIZE, not a constant. Followed into
the Ethanon source, which Enhanced's own rules call the only trustworthy spec:
- the script's GetSize binds to ETHScriptEntity::GetCurrentSize
(ETHScriptObjRegister.generic.cpp:222 and :358). There is no GetSize member;
- ETHSpriteEntity::GetCurrentSize (ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:652) returns
m_pSprite->GetFrameSize() * m_properties.scale;
- antiportal.ent draws white_ring.png with SpriteCut 1x1, and that image is
128 x 128 - so the frame is the whole of it;
- SGlobalScale::scaleEntity multiplies m_properties.scale by the node's own
`scale` custom data, and the scene-wide pass that calls it scales every
entity that does not carry `scalable = 0`. No antiportal carries one.
GetSize().x is that 128 x the node's `scale` x the manager's Scale(0.5) (`manager`
below): the ring is 64 x scale units ACROSS, and the circle a tap is refused in is
half of that, a RADIUS OF 32 x scale. An earlier reading of this block took
128 x 0.5 = 64 x scale for the radius: it missed the manager's Scale(0.5) and was
2x too big (64 x scale is the ring's diameter, never its radius). Footage F3
refutes it as it refutes the Godot project's 16 (`_measured` below).
AntiPortalManager::AntiPortalManager (bytes 104925..105343): instructions 16-37
collect GetEntityArray('antiportal') and GetEntityArray('antiportal.ent') into
`fields`, and for each field (loop 40-103) SetUInt('elapsedTime', 0) (48-60),
SetColor(vector3(1, 0, 0)) (65-80) and Scale(0.5f) (83-92: PshC4 0.5f ...
CALLSYS ETHEntity::Scale). ETHEntity::Scale(float) multiplies m_properties.scale
(ETHEntity.cpp:591-597, its particle systems with it; antiportal.ent has none),
and both the draw and the field test read GetCurrentSize, frame x
m_properties.scale (ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:652-685; the draw ETHRenderEntity.cpp:122,
the test isPointInAntiPortalField, bytes 334800..335020, instructions 14-17).
Game::preLoop scales every entity by its node's `scale` (instruction 37) before
it builds the manager (85); both multiply, so the order does not matter.
So the ring is 128 x 0.5 x node scale units across, 64 x scale, and the circle
a tap is refused in is half of that, 32 x scale: one circle, drawn and played.
`entity` is the name the manager collects, both spellings (a level's
anti_portal_agent and no_portal zones are not its fields and keep their size).
`scale` multiplies the node's own `scale` in the port's picture (the layer's
DrawnSprite::scale, the static portal's 0.8 channel).

_radius_source: DECODED, AND PLAYED since the remaster record's step 127 (00_order R1, the owner's
standing ruling: what the original does). white_ring.png's 128 x the manager's
Scale(0.5) x isPointInAntiPortalField's 0.5 (`_source`), in units per unit of the
node's own `scale`, which Portals::State::Holds multiplies it by. The port played the
Godot project's guess of 16 here, half the original's field, until step 127.
Every field is ONE circle, drawn and played: the ring the layer draws, 128 x
manager.scale x the node's scale across, is twice this radius x the node's scale.
A `no_portal` node was in the port's no_portal_zone role and tested with this
radius too, though AntiPortalManager gathers only antiportal and antiportal.ent
(`manager`). The game places one, 1-07's no_portal_705 at (232, 194): its 32 u lay
wholly inside antiportal_687's 96 u field (56 u between the centres, 56 + 32 < 96),
so it refused no tap the antiportal did not. Since planning step 156 it is in
scenery_hint (data/entity_roles.json) and refuses nothing, as the original's does:
_measured: antiportal_687 at (288, 192), scale 3, the player still at the spawn and every ray
clear: taps 35.6, 78.7, 93.9 and 94.9 u from its centre were refused (red_waves
each time), taps 97.1 and 98.1 u were accepted and opened a portal. The refusal
the port played is refuted by the refusals at 78.7-94.9 u.
The same level's projectile blocker anti_projectile_wall_ent_743 at (313, 185) has
its corners inside the 96 u field (farthest 91.1 u), but F3 (6.3) shows it kills a
shot aimed PAST the field's right edge, which the field alone allows: test_mp_shot's
blocker case lands its shot at (380, 150), 101 u from the field's centre, outside it.

_source: ETHCallback_anti_portal_agent (AntiPortalManager.angelscript, bytes 336011..337087), the
callback of both spellings (00_order 8.0 rule 4), every frame the agent is run:
#4-9     pos = GetPositionXY()
#11-22   halfSize = GetSize() x 0.7f  (despite its name: 0.7 of the whole size)
#24-35   getEntitiesFromNeighbourBuckets(GetBucket(pos), ...): what is round it
#49-59   itself is passed over
#61-77   only an entity named 'projectile.ent': the portal shot
#79-108  only while it is still in flight: squaredDistance(its position, its
'casterPos') < its 'squaredDistance', the square of the way it was fired
#110-124 within halfSize.x of the agent: squaredDistance < halfSize.x ^ 2
#126-142 DeleteEntity(the shot), DeleteEntity(itself)
#144-166 AddScaledEntity('antiportal_explosion.ent', vector3(pos, scale(32)),
getScale()) (effects.json antiportal_explosion)
#168-177 deleteAntiPortalInThisBucket(GetBucket(pos), pos, true)
#179-181 startEarthquake(20, 100) (earthquake.json agent_killed)
#183-187 playExplosionSound(true) (sounds.json playExplosionSound(true))
#189-190 and no other shot is looked at this frame.
The agent's own test is nothing more: anti_portal_agent.ent is shape 0 (no body) and
AntiPortalManager never gathers it (entity_roles.json no_portal_zone), so it refuses
no tap and stops nothing a shot is not killed by.
size_units is GetSize().x, ETHSpriteEntity::GetCurrentSize = frame x scale
(ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:652): entities/anti_portal_agent.png is 32 x 32 by its PNG header,
SpriteCut 1 x 1, <Scale> 1, and no agent of the 21 carries a `scale` of its own, so
0.7 x 32 = 22.4 units. The node's `scale`, where one had it, would multiply it
(SGlobalScale::scaleEntity).
deleteAntiPortalInThisBucket(bucket, agentPos, seekNeighbours) (bytes 335206..336011):
#4-7     GetEntitiesFromBucket(bucket), in the bucket's own order
#13-33   an entity whose GetEntityName() is exactly 'antiportal' - ring_entity, the
BARE spelling only: an antiportal.ent is never deleted here
#35-47   whose field holds agentPos (isPointInAntiPortalField, the field test a tap
is refused by; a dead one holds nothing)
#49-65   DeleteEntity(it) and true: ONE ring, the first
#75-172  else, with seekNeighbours, the same once in each of bucket - (1, 0),
+ (1, 0), - (0, 1), + (0, 1), without seeking further (seek_neighbours, in
that order: 00_order 8.0 rule 3, arguments pushed last-first)
#173-176 else false: no ring goes.
bucket_units: GetBucket is floor(pos / bucketSize) (ETHBucketManager.cpp:47-50), and
Game::start's four-string LoadScene pushes no bucket size, so it is
_ETH_DEFAULT_BUCKET_SIZE, 256 (ETHTypes.h:58; ETHScriptWrapper.generic.cpp:314). Whether
the shipped engine buckets the .esc's own coordinates or the screen's is the remaster
record's open question (its draw-order step); it changes no answer here: on all 21
agents the ring deleted is the same at 256, 256 / 1.5 and 256 / 2.8125, and at a field
of 16 or 32 x scale (out/parity/program/R17/agent_census.txt).
_measured: footage F17 (out/parity/footage/F17.md 1.1-1.2), 4-01 (level0c): a shot from about
the projectile is at the agent near #36 (2.167 s), antiportal_explosion bursts #44-#52,
and the pink field of antiportal_2108 is gone by #60 (3.25 s).
_not_modelled: The agent is a static entity (anti_portal_agent.ent static 1), and Ethanon runs a static
entity's callback only while its bucket is drawn. The port tests every agent every
tick. A shot flies from the player to a tap, both on screen, and dies within 22.4 u of
an agent, so the agent's bucket is on screen in every case but an agent within 22.4 u of
the view's edge whose 256 u bucket lies wholly outside it.
BUILT in planning step 149 (G4): the shot flies as ETHCallback_projectile does, and an
agent tests its POSITION once a frame, as the original's static callback does: on the
tick a tap fires it (the projectile is added by `loop`, after the dynamic callbacks, so
this frame's static pass finds it where it was spawned: at the player's centre), then on
its first callback at 24 + 3.2 u out - never in between - then every 3.2 u (shot.json
`flight`). So an agent within 22.4 u of the PLAYER still dies at once (the static pass of
the tap's own frame sees the shot at its spawn, short of the end of its way); one that
only the first hop's line passes near does not, and a shot that arrives on a callback
is deleted before any static callback of that frame looks (DeleteEntity erases it from its
bucket at once, ETHBucketManager.cpp:434-476), so an agent it would first come within
22.4 u of at the end of its way is not met.
